speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Miss Cheryl Chan1 has also asked a related question for a subsequent Sitting.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When we look at these questions, it is useful, first, to consider how extensive the use of cladding is in Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you look at it from 1985, based on building plans submitted, less than 20% of these building projects used cladding.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you look at composite materials, they typically comprise two non-flammable layers with a core material sandwiched between the two non-combustible layers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Fire Code requirements for these composite panels when they are used as cladding on external walls accepts three internationally recognised testing standards, the EN 13501-1, which is the European standard, the BS 476 group of tests, which is British standard, and the United States (US) standard, NFPA 285.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In this case, the BS 476 tests were applied.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For composite panels used as cladding on external walls, in order to meet the Fire Code requirement when using this British standard, you take the core material of the panels, and they have to be tested on their own.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When they are tested on their own, they must meet Class "0" standard.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When the core material is ignited on its own, the fire must not spread along the surface.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, whenever I refer to Class "0" standard or Class "0" on core standard, I am referring to this British standard, and the equivalent under the US and European testing standards.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, going to Miss Chan's question on conformance of building materials with fire safety standards that are stipulated, it works in this way.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If you have a building project, you will have appointed registered architects or professional engineers.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They are responsible for selecting the correct materials, appropriate materials and products which comply with the Fire Code.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: On top of that, there is an independent Registered Inspector who is required to inspect the building when completed.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Only then will the Singapore Civil Defence Force (SCDF) issue a Fire Safety Certificate, because every premises must get the certificate before the premises can be used or occupied.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Some material will require testing to ensure that they meet the Fire Code requirements, like composite panels.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They will have to be certified by local Certification Bodies.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: How do the Certification Bodies go about it?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: They will accept test results from accredited testing laboratories, which can be either overseas or in Singapore.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If they are overseas, there is a certain number of them, which is accredited by us, accepted by us.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: The Certification Bodies also will have to conduct periodic audits to ensure that certified products continue to conform to those standards.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Of course, if you carry out any work which is unauthorised or if you allow any unauthorised works which have an impact on fire safety, that will be an offence and attracting fines of up to $200,000 or imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SCDF will take action against QPs and Registered Inspectors if they have not carried out their duties properly.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In respect of 30 Toh Guan Road fire on 4 May, investigations were conducted.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When my Ministry discovered this, we decided to check how many other buildings had been supplied with Alubond cladding by the same distributor.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That distributor happens to be the sole local distributor of this material.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We took the approach that, with the exception of those that tested compliant, as long as the building had public access, and even if the cladding was low, 3% of the external wall, we will still identify it.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we took a very zero-tolerance approach, because we felt the public ought to know.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Since 24 August, and as of 8 September, more buildings have been tested and more QPs have contacted SCDF.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As of 8 September, there are 37 buildings that may have used Alubond composite panels as cladding on their walls.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As I said, these 15 range from 3% to higher but, mostly, it is, if my memory serves me right, less than 25%.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will set out what we know so far.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: What we know is that the distributor had sold two models of Alubond composite panels.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: One meets the Class "0" on core requirement for use as cladding on external walls, while the other model does not.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It appears that stocks of both models may have been mixed together at the distributor's local warehouse.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: As a result, I think non-Class "0" on core composite panels may have, at times, been supplied for use on the external walls of buildings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It does not mean that all the panels would have been non-compliant, but some may have been non-compliant, or are non-compliant.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And there seems to be a second reason.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: It appears that the composite panels which were certified to be Class "0" on core were not of uniformly same quality; some met the standard, but others did not.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, we are investigating if this is a manufacturing issue.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In summary, on this point, it appears that non-compliant claddings may have been installed for a mix of these two reasons.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For the public to understand, in addition to requirements on claddings, we have very strict fire safety requirements to minimise fire-spread and protect occupants.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Those requirements, for example, fire-resistant floors, fire-resistant walls, exits which have to meet certain requirements − all of these, put together, will help us assess the fire safety of a building.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SCDF's assessment is that those buildings remain fit and safe for occupancy and they have adequate safety provisions, including other fire protection systems.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: SCDF has also required the building owners to check their fire safety systems to make sure they are in good order.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, while the claddings are being removed, to enhance the vigilance of their personnel, remove any fire hazards.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked if SCDF has checked whether lifts under the —

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I am taking three questions together plus one.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Er Dr Lee asked if SCDF has checked whether lifts under the Lift Upgrading Programme use non-Class "0" on core cladding.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Actually, the vast majority of Housing and Development Board blocks do not use cladding, or use only non-combustible cladding.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We will work with the relevant agencies, building industry, to review the processes.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: If they have any doubt whatsoever that the cladding is Class "0" on core standard, they have been advised to send in the samples for tests by an accredited testing laboratory.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh asked if there are plans to conduct a more thorough testing/extensive audit of all claddings.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: I have set out what has been done and what reminders have been sent, for example, to QPs and Registered Inspectors.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But in order to understand this, you have to understand how the testing is done and what the processes are.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: For example, it is not possible to test every panel because, if you understand testing, it requires burning of the panel.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: So, by definition, if you test every panel, there will be no panels left to install.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: That is why sampling remains the international standard.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: In addition to what has been done, we are also looking beyond the projects supplied by the distributor of the Alubond composite panels.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: We are reviewing them based on the testing that has been done, to consider whether any further steps will be necessary.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: But I have indicated to Members the two preliminary views on two possible reasons as to why this might have happened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: When we have completed the investigations, we will relook at that to see whether anything else needs to be done.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: At the same time, when something like this happens, we need to find out why it happened.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Is it because the rules were not adequate?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Or is it because of a specific set of human errors which could not have been prevented by the rules?

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And, if so, then whether some additional rules are necessary.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: Once we have completed the investigations, we will consider what further steps, if any, are necessary.

speaker: Mr K Shanmugam
text: And if Members of the House have any other suggestions, they can send them to my Ministry.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
